- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 1–2% upward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 0.67–1.00) correlate with overconfidence in model; apply 2–3% downward adjustment if sentiment >0.50 and price is trending up.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00–0.20) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
